## Stationary Classical Correspondence

The native construction has now separated three things: the SI source packages, the achieved stationary scalar map, and the narrower carrier and directional realizations. Classical correspondence can therefore test each layer without turning classical variables into M1's primitive language.

### Source-density calibration

The even source is a momentum-content density,

$$
[\mathcal M]=\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}m^{-2}},
$$

whereas ordinary mass density has units kg m$^{-3}$. Cold static matter therefore calibrates as

$$
\boxed{\mathcal M=c\rho}.
$$

The convenient mass-density-form variable is $\rho_M=\mathcal M/c$. The first and second carrier moments may be assembled into the correspondence matrix

$$
P^{\mu\nu}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathcal M & \mathcal P_j\\
\mathcal P_i & \mathcal C_{ij}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
T^{\mu\nu}=cP^{\mu\nu}.
$$

Thus, componentwise,

$$
T^{00}=c\mathcal M,
\qquad
T^{0i}=c\mathcal P_i,
\qquad
T^{ij}=c\mathcal C_{ij}.
$$

This is a correspondence matrix, not a new source ontology. Its entries are moments of one local momentum content: scalar/even content, net directional imbalance, and directional transport coupling. The stationary scalar construction uses $\mathcal M$ as its achieved source. The provisional directional response uses $\mathcal P_i$. The matrix simply shows how those native packages face familiar energy, current, and stress components after the M1 source grammar is already in place.

### Newtonian recovery

The stationary scalar equation is

$$
\Delta\theta_0
=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}\mathcal M.
$$

With $\mathcal M=c\rho$ and

$$
U:=-c^2\theta_0,
$$

it becomes

$$
\boxed{\Delta U=4\pi G_N\rho}.
$$

For a spherical exterior source of mass $M$,

$$
U(r)=-\frac{G_NM}{r},
\qquad
\theta_0(r)=\frac{G_NM}{c^2r},
$$

and hence

$$
G(r)=\sqrt{1-\frac{2G_NM}{c^2r}}
=1+\frac U{c^2}+O(U^2/c^4).
$$

The Poisson equation, Newtonian potential, and leading clock-redshift slope form the achieved stationary correspondence. The exact square root belongs to the selected clock package; it is not an exact Schwarzschild or nonlinear spatial derivation.

This is the scalar clock-depth correspondence. It checks that the additive part of the directional source channels produces the usual Newtonian weak-field limit without importing classical density as the primitive M1 source.

The dimensional calibration, potential dictionary, and weak-light target are collected in [Appendix 3.6A](#sec-derivation-03-06A-stationary-correspondence).

### Spatial and light targets

In the weak isotropic comparison,

$$
d\ell^2
=\left(1-2\gamma\frac{U}{c^2}\right)
\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j.
$$

The leading light coefficients are

$$
\delta\phi
=2(1+\gamma)\frac{G_NM}{bc^2},
$$

and

$$
\Delta t_{\mathrm{Shapiro}}
=\frac{(1+\gamma)G_NM}{c^3}
\ln(\text{endpoint geometry}).
$$

The observed values require $\gamma=1$ [@will2014confrontation]. Chapter 3 therefore keeps the standard bending and Shapiro results as correspondence requirements. The carrier analysis of the previous section explains why they are not yet predictions of a content-only reciprocal M1 action: within the declared shell and response class, the $\gamma=1$ ruler brings a matching stress-trace scalar source.

### Directional and rotating-source targets

Given SI, the odd source is the current:

$$
\mathcal P_i=j_i.
$$

The provisional transverse response is

$$
\Delta\theta_i^\perp
=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^3}j_i^\perp.
$$

In the familiar stationary gauge-fixed comparison, the target shift equation is

$$
\Delta A_i
=\frac{16\pi G_N}{c^3}j_i^\perp,
\qquad
\partial_iA_i=0.
$$

This equation is a calibration target, not the M1 source law. The current $j_i$ enters because SI has already supplied $\mathcal P_i=j_i$. The transverse condition also reminds us that not every raw directional distribution is automatically a stationary shift input.

If the observer-facing package is written as

$$
A_i=-\kappa_A\theta_i^\perp,
$$

then $\kappa_A=4$ would reproduce the target coefficient. The issue is not whether that number can be inserted. It is whether one positive causal action fixes its magnitude and sign while also supplying reciprocal work and observer transport. The present construction has not yet done so.

For a compact slow rotating source with angular momentum $\mathbf J$,

$$
\theta_i^{\mathrm{rot}}
=\frac{G_N}{2c^3}
\frac{(\mathbf J\times\mathbf r)_i}{r^3}.
$$

Weak Kerr and Lense--Thirring comparison require

$$
h_{0i}^{\mathrm{GR}}
=-\frac{2G_N}{c^3}
\frac{(\mathbf J\times\mathbf r)_i}{r^3}
=-4\theta_i^{\mathrm{rot}}.
$$

Thus a future physical directional map must reach

$$
\boxed{\lvert\kappa_A\rvert=4}
$$

with the observed orientation [@ciufolini2004confirmation; @everitt2011gravity]. This endpoint is precise enough to reject incorrect closures, but it does not itself supply one. The positive one-vector action reaches the magnitude with the opposite physical orientation; an elliptic constrained response can fit the stationary sign only by choosing an undetermined coefficient and supplies no causal observer transport.

A boosted static metric gives a useful conditional relation. Take

$$
h_{00}=2\theta_0,
\qquad
h_{ij}=2\sigma\theta_0\delta_{ij},
$$

Under the normalized weak clock convention, the carrier/ruler coefficient and the boosted-metric coefficient describe the same spatial slope, $\sigma=\gamma$. The separate symbols keep their two roles visible.

If the odd-source convention is $\mathcal P_i=\eta j_i$, first-order boost consistency yields

$$
\boxed{
\kappa_A\eta=2(1+\sigma)}.
$$

SI gives $\eta=1$, and the standard spatial target gives $\sigma=1$, so the relation lands on $\kappa_A=4$. The agreement shows that the source normalization, weak spatial target, boost relation, and rotating endpoint are mutually compatible. It does not turn them into one derived source--action--observer pipeline. Kerr and Lense--Thirring therefore remain weak stationary correspondence targets; Chapter 3 has neither an exact Kerr pullback nor a native rotating-source solution.

The endpoint sign audit and the conditional boost identity are developed in [Appendix 3.6B](#sec-derivation-03-06B-frame-drag-audit) and [Appendix 3.6C](#sec-derivation-03-06C-boost-consistency).

### A conserved radiation cavity

Source apportioning becomes physically visible only when a complete conserved system is compared. Consider uniform isotropic radiation of total energy $U$ confined within a thin spherical wall of inner radius $R$. The radiation pressure is $p=u/3$. Mechanical equilibrium requires the wall's tangential tension magnitude to be

$$
\tau=\frac{pR}{2}
=\frac{U}{8\pi R^2}.
$$

Radiation pressure and wall tension then satisfy, axis by axis,

$$
\int T^{ii}\,d^3x=0
\qquad\text{(no sum)}.
$$

This is a complete conserved source, not a photon gas treated apart from its container. Both the linearized GR ledger and SI plus the minimal stationary M1 map give the same exterior monopole,

$$
\Theta_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)
=\frac{G_N(E_{\mathrm w}+U)}{c^4r},
$$

where $E_{\mathrm w}$ is the wall energy. The difference lies inside. GR's stationary lapse responds to $T^{00}+T^{kk}$, while the minimal M1 scalar map reads the content density once and assigns no independent response to $\mathcal C_{ij}$.

Compare a static clock at the center with one at the inner wall. With the stationary clock field normalized at infinity,

$$
1+z_{c\to R}=\frac{N(R)}{N(0)}.
$$

At leading weak-field order, the two descriptions give

$$
z_{c\to R}^{\mathrm{GR}}
=\frac{G_NU}{c^4R},
$$

$$
z_{c\to R}^{\mathrm{M1}}
=\frac{G_NU}{2c^4R}.
$$

Thus SI plus the current minimal stationary field/readout map predicts half the GR center-to-inner-wall shift for this cavity. The wall energy contributes equally to the two selected clock locations and cancels from the ratio; the exterior field remains unchanged.

This is one controlled conditional discriminator, not a generic theorem that pressure always gravitates by half. It depends on SI, the minimal scalar response, and the present allocation of the complete source. An independently derived scalar response to $\mathcal C_{ij}$ could change or remove the difference, and a complete M1 wall and binding ledger remains open. The scale also makes a direct laboratory test infeasible:

$$
\lvert\Delta z\rvert
\simeq4.13\times10^{-45}
\frac{U/\mathrm J}{R/\mathrm m}.
$$

For $U=1$ MJ and $R=1$ m, the difference is about $4.1\times10^{-39}$. No external novelty claim is made for the result.

The complete-source ledger, paired clock ratio, robustness conditions, and scale estimate are derived in [Appendix 3.6D](#sec-derivation-03-06D-radiation-cavity).

### Metric-facing dictionary

For comparison with familiar stationary geometry, take $x^0=ct$, so the mixed metric perturbation is dimensionless. The weak-field dictionary may then be written schematically as

$$
g_{00}=-(1+2U/c^2),
$$

and

$$
g_{0i}\sim A_i.
$$

The first relation reads the scalar package as the clock-depth side of the geometry. The second reserves the shift potential for the mixed directional side. Its sign and coefficient depend on the comparison convention and on the still-unclosed observer map.

A stationary rotating target such as Kerr is useful because it sharply exhibits the same split: scalar clocking and an azimuthal shift appear as distinct pieces of one stationary gravitational structure. Here that remains a weak stationary comparison. The chapter does not possess an exact Kerr pullback or a native rotating-source derivation.

### Local clock and transport comparison

The scalar carrier block also has a stationary clock reading. In M1 variables,

$$
d\tau=N\,dt_*,
\qquad
d\ell^2=Q^{-1}\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j.
$$

For two static clocks, $1+z_{a\to b}=N(b)/N(a)$. Gravity-side clock dressing and motion-side slowing therefore remain distinct even when a later comparison writes them in one proper-time expression.

The provisional directional bookkeeping,

$$
\Pi_i=p_i-p_{f,c}A_i,
$$

has the expected structural place in a dragged local frame, but it is not yet a derived universal generator. Correspondence identifies the endpoint a completed observer map must reach; it does not promote the diagnostic notation by resemblance alone.

### What correspondence establishes

The stationary scalar construction reaches classical gravity where it is strongest:

$$
\mathcal M=c\rho,
\qquad
\theta_0=-U/c^2,
\qquad
\Delta U=4\pi G_N\rho.
$$

The standard $\gamma=1$ light response, boost identity, and $|\kappa_A|=4$ rotating endpoint define the next correspondence targets rather than a completed derivation. The conserved cavity then shows what the current source choice would mean in one interior comparison while leaving the exterior monopole untouched. These distinctions keep correspondence useful: it validates the achieved scalar engine, sharpens the unclosed spatial and directional burdens, and identifies one conditional place where source apportioning matters.
